issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for fields numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents: the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares these two attributes as type double, whereas the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares them as int. The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) directs students to add attributes from the UML, which will encourage them to use double. This inconsistency can confuse students about which numeric type to use, and may lead to mismatched constructor signatures and incorrect return/operation types in methods that use these attributes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the numeric types consistent across problem statement, template instructions, and solution. Preferred fix: change the UML and problem text to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (counts are integers), and update any examples/notes accordingly. Alternatively, if doubles are required, update the solution and template to use double for these fields and adjust method return types/implementations (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents) to handle/return the appropriate numeric type. Also ensure the constructor parameter types and any example toString formatting match the chosen type.
